[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Advanced Data Integrity in PostgreSQL: Constraints, Triggers, and Generated Columns"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Maintaining data integrity is critical for robust database applications. PostgreSQL provides multiple layers of defense to ensure your data remains accurate and consistent. This tutorial explores three powerful mechanisms: Constraints, Triggers, and Generated Columns."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Declarative Constraints"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Constraints are the first line of defense. They are declaratively defined on tables and enforced automatically by the database engine during INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE employees (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    last_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE,
    age INT CHECK (age >= 18),
    department_id INT,
    CONSTRAINT fk_department
        FOREIGN KEY (department_id)
        REFERENCES departments(id)
        ON DELETE SET NULL
);"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"PRIMARY KEY: Ensures uniqueness and non-nullability for row identification."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"UNIQUE: Prevents duplicate values across specified columns."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"CHECK: Validates custom boolean expressions on a per-row basis."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Generated Columns"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generated columns are special columns whose values are computed automatically from an expression involving other columns in the same table. PostgreSQL supports stored generated columns, which compute values on writes and consume storage like regular columns."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE rectangles (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    width NUMERIC NOT NULL,
    height NUMERIC NOT NULL,
    area NUMERIC GENERATED ALWAYS AS (width * height) STORED
);"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"When you insert rows into the rectangles table, you only provide the width and height. PostgreSQL calculates the area automatically."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"INSERT INTO rectangles (width, height) VALUES (5.0, 10.0);
SELECT * FROM rectangles;"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Triggers and Procedural Logic"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"When declarative constraints and generated columns are not enough, triggers allow you to execute custom PL/pgSQL functions automatically in response to database events (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE)."},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, create the trigger function that updates a modification timestamp:"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION update_modified_column()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    NEW.updated_at = NOW();
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ language 'plpgsql';"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, attach this function to a table using a BEFORE UPDATE trigger."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE documents (
    id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    title TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TRIGGER set_timestamp
BEFORE UPDATE ON documents
FOR EACH ROW
EXECUTE FUNCTION update_modified_column();"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining constraints for strict rules, generated columns for derived data, and triggers for complex auditing or side effects, you can build a highly resilient database architecture directly inside PostgreSQL."}]
